title: Hidden chirality and half-vortex formation in exciton-polariton condensates
authors: A. N. Osipov, I. Y. Chestnov, P. G. Lagoudakis, A. V. Yulin
abstract: We show that a radially symmetric, nonresonantly pumped spinor exciton-polariton condensate can acquire chirality without a rotating drive, chiral geometry, or pump orbital angular momentum. Spin relaxation in a two-reservoir system shifts the reservoir-induced blueshift relative to the gain profile, creating an effective non-Hermitian chiral potential. A reduced angular-mode theory reveals tunable exceptional points and non-reciprocal coupling between counter-rotating modes. Full driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that this hidden chirality enables all-optical formation of spin-selective half-vortices.
summary: The paper reveals that exciton-polariton condensates can spontaneously develop chirality due to spin relaxation effects within the coupled reservoir system. This hidden non-Hermitian potential allows for the controlled, all-optical creation of half-vortices, where polarization components exhibit distinct topological winding numbers.
main_problem: The study demonstrates how a spinor exciton-polariton condensate can spontaneously acquire chirality without external chiral driving fields.
main_result: This hidden chirality enables the all-optical formation of spin-selective half-vortices, where one polarization component acquires a definite phase winding while the other remains near zero winding.
method: The analysis uses adiabatic elimination of fast reservoir dynamics to derive an effective non-Hermitian potential and subsequently analyzes coupled angular-mode equations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii equation for the spinor order parameter, incorporating coupling to two distinct excitonic reservoirs (active and inactive).
key_observables: Spin-selective vorticity ($\sigma-$ component showing $2\pi$ winding vs. $\sigma+$ zero-winding), time-averaged angular momentum ($\langle m_\pm angle_t$), and the existence of Exceptional Points (EPs).
important_parameters: The relative phase shift between reservoir blueshifts, pump modulation depth ($ho$), and parameters governing non-reciprocal coupling near EPs.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on adiabatic elimination of fast reservoir dynamics and approximations derived from low polariton densities in some theoretical sections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mechanism (Fig. 1), show half-vortex states ($\sigma-$ winding vs $\sigma+$ dipole) (Fig. 2), map out angular momentum bistability near EPs (Fig. 3), and confirm robustness against fast oscillations from TE-TM splitting (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical mechanism of hidden chirality via spin relaxation to deriving simplified coupled-mode equations, analyzing spectral features like Exceptional Points, and finally simulating the resulting half-vortex formation.
why_interesting: This work provides a clean theoretical framework for generating topological structures (vortices) in quantum optical systems using internal degrees of freedom (spin/polarization) rather than external geometric controls, which is highly relevant to advanced quantum light sources and nonlinear optics.

(b) Corresponding time evolution on the op- posite side of the same EP. The splitting induces fast spin- orbit oscillations between the two circular components.
